title: Salesforce CLI, VS Code, project structure, manifests, retrieve, deploy, and validate
objectives: Describe a Salesforce DX project: sfdx-project.json, package directories, source format versus metadata format, and .forceignore.
Choose retrieve versus deploy versus validate and name the matching Salesforce CLI project commands.
Explain manifests (package.xml), --metadata, and --source-dir as mutually exclusive ways to name a payload.
State that project commands must run inside a project, that production never allows source tracking, and that validate is intended for production rather than sandbox dry-runs.
diagnostic_question: You have a DX project, a sandbox with a new LAB_ Apex class, and a production window tonight. Which CLI command retrieves the class, which deploys it, which validates without saving, and what would you refuse to pass on production?
definition: Salesforce CLI project commands synchronize metadata between a local DX project and an org. Retrieve copies metadata from the org into the project (source format by default). Deploy pushes local metadata to the org. Validate checks a metadata deployment without executing it, returning a job ID that can later drive a quick deploy. A DX project is identified by sfdx-project.json, which names package directories and related configuration. ([Project Setup](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_workspace_setup.htm); [project retrieve start](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_project_retrieve_start.html); [project deploy validate](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_project_deploy_validate.html))
why_it_matters: Wrong command direction overwrites the only good copy. Validate-on-sandbox cargo-cult skips the documented sandbox dry-run path. --ignore-errors on production can leave an inconsistent org. Interviewers want the verbs retrieve, deploy, and validate, plus manifest versus metadata versus source-dir.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of an air-traffic control desk. VS Code is the radar screen. Salesforce CLI is the radio. The DX project is the controlled airspace map (sfdx-project.json says where the map folders live). Retrieve is inbound traffic from the org. Deploy is clearance to land local files on the org. Validate is a dry-run clearance that does not land the flight. package.xml is the flight strip that lists which aircraft move. Never issue a production landing with ignore-errors. Production towers do not offer source tracking.
deeper_explanation: A Salesforce DX project provides structure for the org's metadata (code and configuration), org templates, sample data, and tests, stored in source control. sfdx-project.json marks the directory as a DX project, lists package directories, and supports second-generation packaging configuration and API version. Source format uses a different set of files than Metadata API format; retrieve stores source format, and deploy converts to the format Metadata API requires. ([Project Setup](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_workspace_setup.htm))

You must run project retrieve/deploy/validate from within a project. Retrieve pulls metadata from an org to the local project. Components retrieve in source format by default; --target-metadata-dir retrieves metadata format into a ZIP. Name the payload with --manifest (package.xml), --metadata, or --source-dir—do not mix manifest with the other two. Production orgs never allow source tracking; scratch and sandbox orgs enable it by default. ([project retrieve start](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_project_retrieve_start.html); [project deploy start](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_project_deploy_start.html))

project deploy validate verifies whether a deployment will succeed without deploying. It is similar to deploy start except Apex tests are required and the command returns a job ID rather than executing the deployment. If validation succeeds, pass that job ID to project deploy quick. The job ID is valid for 10 days. Do not use this command on sandboxes; sandboxes do not run tests during a deploy by default. To validate with tests on a sandbox, use project deploy start --dry-run --test-level RunLocalTests. ([project deploy validate](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_project_deploy_validate.html))

Deploy flags that interviews catch: never use --ignore-errors when deploying to production (partial success can leave an inconsistent org). --ignore-conflicts applies only to source-tracked orgs and has no effect on production. --dry-run validates and can run tests without saving. --pre-destructive-changes and --post-destructive-changes point at delete manifests (DEVOPS-009). Salesforce Extensions for VS Code wrap the same CLI/project model; the commands remain the contract. Convert between metadata format and source format with project convert when a repo started as a Metadata API retrieve.

mental_model.analogy: An air-traffic control desk: CLI radio, VS Code radar, DX project airspace map, package.xml flight strip, retrieve inbound, deploy landing clearance, validate dry-run clearance that does not land.
useful_mapping: sfdx-project.json → which folders are controlled airspace (package directories)
source format → how the local map is filed
metadata format / ZIP → the bag Metadata API actually loads
package.xml manifest → the flight strip listing components
retrieve → inbound copy from the org
deploy → land local metadata on the org
validate → dry-run for production, job ID later used with quick deploy
VS Code extensions → radar UI over the same radio commands
where_it_breaks: Production never offers source tracking; a tower with no conflict radar still accepts deploy/retrieve if you name the payload.
Validate is not the sandbox dry-run path; use deploy start --dry-run there.
The analogy does not encode Apex test levels or 75% coverage.
--ignore-errors is a dangerous partial landing, not a weather workaround.

Two-minute interview: project structure, source vs metadata format, retrieve vs deploy vs validate.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: A DX project is sfdx-project.json plus package directories. Retrieve copies metadata down; deploy pushes it up; validate checks a production-style deploy without saving and yields a 10-day job ID. Name the payload with one of manifest, metadata, or source-dir. Never ignore-errors on production.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from the project, not from random folders. I pick retrieve when the org has the change, deploy when Git has it. For production I prefer validate then quick deploy when the window is long. For sandboxes I use dry-run with RunLocalTests, not validate. I do not mix --manifest with --metadata. I treat VS Code as a UI over the same commands.

terminology.non_example: The mdapi ZIP produced by --target-metadata-dir, which is metadata format.

terminology.plain: package.xml listing which metadata components to retrieve or deploy.

terminology.plain: Push local metadata to the org and save it (unless dry-run).

terminology.non_example: Using validate against a developer sandbox because it 'sounds safer.'

When a production window needs project deploy validate and a later quick deploy rather than a long test run in the freeze.
When a sandbox needs a dry-run deploy with tests, which is not the validate command.

decision_table.signal: The org has a Setup change that must enter Git.
decision_table.choose: sf project retrieve start with a named payload.
decision_table.not: Deploy first, which would push stale local files.
decision_table.why: Retrieve copies metadata from the org into the project in source format.

decision_table.signal: Git has reviewed metadata that must land in a sandbox.
decision_table.not: project deploy validate as the sandbox tool.
decision_table.why: Validate is documented for production-style checks, not sandbox defaults.

decision_table.signal: Production needs a long test run before a short go-live window.
decision_table.choose: project deploy validate, keep the job ID up to 10 days, then project deploy quick.
decision_table.not: Starting a full test deploy only after the freeze starts with no validation job.
decision_table.why: Validate returns a job ID for a quicker later deploy that skips rerunning those tests.

decision_table.signal: You want tests without saving on a sandbox.
decision_table.not: project deploy validate on that sandbox.
decision_table.why: The validate command reference says not to use it on sandboxes.

decision_table.signal: A production deploy fails some components and someone suggests ignoring errors.
decision_table.choose: Fix the payload and redeploy as an all-or-nothing production deploy.
decision_table.why: The flag can deploy some components and skip others, leaving an inconsistent production org.

interview_questions.question: What is a Salesforce DX project, and which CLI verbs move metadata?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A folder with sfdx-project.json and package directories of source-format metadata. Retrieve copies from the org, deploy pushes to the org, validate checks without saving.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I mention source format versus Metadata API format and that deploy converts. I name three selectors: manifest, metadata, source-dir, exclusive with manifest. I say commands must run inside the project. VS Code is optional UI. I do not mix this with Git branching.
interview_questions.example: sf project retrieve start --metadata ApexClass:LAB_GateService from a sandbox into force-app.

interview_questions.question: When do you retrieve versus deploy?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Retrieve when the org has the metadata you want in Git. Deploy when the project has the metadata you want in the org. Name the payload; production has no source tracking.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I ask which side is truth after DEVOPS-001. Admin built a field in sandbox: retrieve. Reviewed PR: deploy. I preview when possible. I never deploy empty local files over org work. I never retrieve hoping Account rows appear.
interview_questions.example: Layout built in Setup → retrieve. Apex written in VS Code → deploy to the scratch org.

interview_questions.question: Production tests take hours. How do validate and quick deploy help?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Run project deploy validate earlier. It does not execute the deploy. Keep the job ID up to 10 days, then project deploy quick in the window.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Validate still requires tests. Quick deploy skips rerunning those tests but overwrites corresponding metadata and does not use source tracking. I would not treat a stale job ID after 10 days as valid. I still need a go/no-go on the validate report. Sandboxes are not this path.
interview_questions.example: Monday validate of force-app against production; Friday quick deploy of that job ID during the CAB window.
tradeoffs: Earlier test cost versus shorter freeze
follow_ups: What if metadata changed after validate?
weak_answer_warnings: Using validate on sandboxes as the same trick

interview_questions.question: A pipeline runs project deploy validate against every sandbox. What do you change?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Stop. The command is not for sandboxes. Use deploy start --dry-run --test-level RunLocalTests there. Keep validate for production-style job IDs.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Sandbox default is not to run tests on deploy, which is why validate is the wrong cargo-cult. Dry-run still does not save. I separate CI jobs by environment class. I cite the validate reference rather than tribal YAML.
interview_questions.example: PR checks against a scratch org use dry-run; the production job uses validate.
tradeoffs: One YAML job versus environment-correct commands
Test time in sandbox versus production
weak_answer_warnings: Leaving validate on sandboxes because it 'sounds safer'

interview_questions.question: Which deploy flags are interview red flags?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Never --ignore-errors on production. Do not expect --ignore-conflicts to work there. Prefer fixing the payload over partial deploys.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: ignore-errors can skip failed components and save the rest, which the CLI warns can make production inconsistent. ignore-conflicts is a source-tracking escape hatch. ignore-warnings is sometimes used in CI with destructive deletes of already-gone components—Needs verification per pipeline, not a production shortcut for real errors. I mention pre/post destructive flags as a pointer to DEVOPS-009.
interview_questions.example: A production deploy with three failures; we roll back the plan rather than ignore-errors.
tradeoffs: Warnings on missing deletes versus hiding compile errors
follow_ups: What is rollbackOnError in Metadata API?

interview_questions.question: How do you name what to retrieve or deploy?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: One family: --manifest package.xml, or --metadata Type:Name, or --source-dir path. Do not mix manifest with the other two.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Manifests are reviewable in PRs. Metadata flags are quick for one class. source-dir is natural for a package directory. Wildcards need quotes. On source-tracked scratch orgs, a flagless deploy/retrieve can mean changed files—but production never has that, so I always can name a payload.
interview_questions.example: sf project deploy start --manifest manifest/lab.xml --target-org uat
tradeoffs: Narrow metadata flag versus whole force-app
follow_ups: How do you generate a manifest from an org?

interview_questions.question: Retrieve seems to do nothing useful from production. Walk it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Production has no source tracking, so a flagless retrieve will not magically know changes. Pass --manifest, --metadata, or --source-dir. Run from the project.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I confirm cwd has sfdx-project.json. I confirm the org alias is production versus sandbox. I check .forceignore. I do not use --package-name as a development retrieve of packaged metadata—the retrieve reference says that output is for reference, not for SCS development. I still will not retrieve business rows.
interview_questions.example: sf project retrieve start --metadata CustomObject:LAB_Gate__c --target-org prod-readonly-alias in a break-glass audit, not as daily source of truth.
tradeoffs: Broad retrieve noise versus tight type list
Production retrieve versus sandbox as the working copy
follow_ups: Why not retrieve managed package internals into Git?

interview_questions.question: Compare Salesforce CLI and VS Code for a DevOps interview.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: VS Code extensions are an optional radar UI. The contract is still a DX project plus retrieve, deploy, and validate. CI will call the CLI, so I learn the commands.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I can demo Org Browser retrieve, but I write pipelines in sf project commands. I know validate versus dry-run regardless of IDE buttons. I do not claim compiler internals. I keep metadata versus data from DEVOPS-001: neither tool is Data Loader.
interview_questions.example: Local: VS Code deploy to scratch. CI: sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --test-level RunLocalTests.
weak_answer_warnings: Saying VS Code replaces the CLI contract
